newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to consider in June freeing capital flows.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to consider in June freeing capital flows.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) will consider lifting restrictions on cross-border capital movements in the second half of June, NBH deputy president Zoltan Bodnar said on Tuesday.
"We will have to decide when we should abolish what and by what method," Bodnar told Reuters during an international conference of monetary experts in Budapest.
Hungary promised to abolish remaining restrictions on capital flow when it joined the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development in March 1996,

Foreign investors are currently only allowed to invest in Hungarian securities which have a maturity of more than one year while their access to the notes of open-ended investment funds and negotiable instruments is also limited.

Hungarian citizens are subject to restrictions on investment in foreign real estate, money markets and negotiable instruments and are not allowed to borrow from abroad for maturities of less than one year. Lending to non-residents of Hungary is also limited.

Bodnar said Hungarian economic fundamentals were strong and there were no threats of neither a capital flight or an excessive capital inflow. However, the country should consider carefully which restrictions it would lift.
"We cannot expose the (international) confidence we have gained to withdrawing any kind of liberalisation step later," Bodnar told the conference.
Bodnar said the Ministry of Justice would submit to the government by the summer recess a draft law which would allow foreign companies to set up branches in Hungary.
He added that the NBH would consider in June what extent of liberalisation was realistic, and how it should happen.
Alternatives include the amendment of the foreign exchange law, the issue of a government decree or the relaxation of licensing rules, he said.

He said he hoped that a decision on liberalising the investments of foreigners in open-ended funds and short-term securities could be made soon, along with the liberalisation of part of the investments of Hungarian abroad.
Bodnar said earlier this month that the NBH would consider in June opening up the foreign exchange forward and futures market to foreign investors.
